name: Label
description: The visible name of a form control, tied to it so that clicking the text focuses the control and screen readers announce the name. Every input, select and textarea needs one.
summary: Visible name of a form control
researchNote: The word "label" is reserved for this

elements.name: Text
elements.description: Names the control in a few words

elements.name: Required marker
elements.description: Marks required or optional fields; its meaning is explained in text

elements.name: Hint
elements.description: Extra guidance under the label, linked to the control with aria-describedby

elements.name: Control
elements.description: The field it names, matched by for and id or nested inside the label

configOptions.options: Separate (for / id), Wraps the control (checkbox, radio)

Hint — guidance under the label

variants.caption: Wraps the control — label after each checkbox
variants.htmlOutline:
<label><input type="checkbox" name="news"> Product news</label>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="tips"> Tips and guides</label>

usageNotes: The name Label is reserved for the form element. For a short category marker use a Tag, and for a status use a Badge.
Connect it with for matching the control's id, or by wrapping the control. Clicking the label then focuses or toggles the control, which also makes small checkboxes easier to hit.
Keep the label visible. Placeholder text is not a label: it disappears when people type and often has low contrast (WCAG 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions).
If the accessible name differs from the visible text, it must contain that text (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name), so voice control users can say what they see.
Mark either the required fields or the optional ones and say what the marker means. Add the required attribute so the requirement is announced.
